reviews.review:
Let’s talk about Varlet

Overall, this game was a complete letdown. I’m genuinely relieved I picked it up on sale instead of paying full price, because even at a discount, it feels overpriced. Realistically this is a $15 $20 game at best.

The experience itself is just….. underwhelming. The story has moments where it starts to get interesting but those moments are quickly interrupted by awkward transitions like the frequent black screens. Instead of showing characters walking away or letting scenes play out naturally the game cuts abruptly which really breaks immersion or even the randomly appearing phones or disappearing phones instead of animating them actually taking out and putting away. 

The music doesn’t help much either it often feels like generic background noise or simply put elevator music, I want something that’s memorable, excites me for battle or exploration not something that makes me yawn and on top of that the gameplay becomes repetitive very quickly such as the enemy designs, they lack variety and both the combat system and the running mechanic feel unnecessarily slow. It’s hard not to wonder where the budget actually went because it certainly doesn’t feel like it was invested in the core elements that make gameplay engaging.

The repeated SSS events are another weak point they become tedious over time though oddly there’s something a bit comforting about their predictability. The dungeon mechanics suffer from the same issue such as repetitive and lacking depth.

That said, the game isn’t without its positives. The character designs are genuinely charming and I enjoyed mechanics like flank attacks and the binding system they add a nice layer to combat. Some of the cutscenes are well done, and the even the anime theme before you start the game presented a nice touch. The first main boss fight stood out as well specifically because of its music it was easily one of the highlights. I also appreciated the bonding system particularly how the game suggests good locations to take characters to build relationships.

However, this leads into one of my biggest disappointments: the so called “romance.” It barely feels like romance at all. As someone who enjoys RPGs with romantic relationship building, it’s frustrating to see the game lean on terms like “intimate” without actually delivering on that promise.

For example, when I tried to pursue a relationship with Sota, it never progressed in a romantic way. Even as I reached Chapter 6 the dynamic remained stuck in a “we’re just bros” loop with him frequently talking about wanting a girlfriend. It felt misleading especially when the game presents these interactions as something deeper. Eventually it seemed like I hit a progression cap with no way to develop the relationship further which is fine if he would you know understand we are suppose to be “dating.”

What makes this more frustrating is how the game handles bonding overall. It gives warnings about getting close to other characters, implying exclusivity yet doesn’t fully commit to making those relationships feel genuinely romantic. Whether this is due to gameplay restrictions or narrative choices or even timing of the game it ultimately hurts immersion. It makes it harder to feel invested in the life you’re building for your character when you already seemed to establish something. 

if a game is going to include a bonding system like this and claims "Intimate bonds" it should fully commit allowing meaningful romantic paths for all characters. As it stands it feels limited and inconsistent. More broadly it would have been great to see the game take more risks with its relationship options instead of playing it so safe.

In the end, I wanted to love this game especially as a Persona fan and the idea that this game would allow Gay romance… I had the idea to simply 100% or even if it was just meh- till I found it that’s impossible in one play through since the game limits hangouts me mechanic and so you’ll have to start a new game to complete the achievements for bonding… oh and  there’s no new game+ option so I just completely lost interest as I reached the last chapter because my interest and immersion just fell apart…. Varlet had potential but it falls short in too many key areas. Between the repetitive gameplay, lackluster execution, and disappointing relationship system, it’s hard to recommend especially at its current price point.
